requirements_inventory.summary: GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}, and a page shows that status.

stack.summary: Proposed: a static HTML page with vanilla JavaScript, served by a small dependency-free Node.js HTTP server (server.js) that uses only built-in modules. The page is a single status display, so it needs no framework or build step. Node is already used by the backend (`node server.js`). The backend base URL comes from an environment variable (BACKEND_BASE_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8000) and reaches the page through a generated /config.js, so it is not hard-coded.

milestones.title: Service status page
milestones.goal: Serve a page that calls GET /health on the configured backend and shows the returned status to the user, with a visible error state if the call fails.

tasks.title: Static server with runtime config
tasks.description: Create package.json with no dependencies and a `test` script that runs `node --test`. Create server.js using node:http. It listens on PORT (default 5173) at host 127.0.0.1 and serves public/index.html at /, public/app.js, and a generated /config.js that sets window.APP_CONFIG = { backendBaseUrl } from the BACKEND_BASE_URL env var (default http://127.0.0.1:8000). Any other path returns 404.

tasks.title: Status page UI
tasks.description: Create public/index.html with a heading 'Service status' and a status element (id="status", role="status", aria-live="polite") that first reads 'Checking…'. Load config.js and then app.js.

tasks.title: Fetch and render health
tasks.description: In public/app.js, on load, send exactly one GET to `${backendBaseUrl}/health`. On a 200 response with JSON {status}, set the status element text to 'Status: ok' (the returned value) and add data-state="ok". On a network error, a non-2xx response, or invalid JSON, show 'Status: unavailable' with data-state="error". Call no other endpoint.

tasks.title: Unit tests
tasks.description: Add node:test tests covering the status rendering logic: an ok response gives 'Status: ok'; a failed fetch or a non-2xx response gives 'Status: unavailable'. Put the logic in a small pure function that can be imported and tested without a browser.

acceptance_criteria.text: Opening http://127.0.0.1:5173/ in a browser shows a heading 'Service status'.
While the backend is running, the page sends GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/health, and within a few seconds the status element (id="status") reads 'Status: ok'.
The only backend request the page makes is GET /health, which matches the operation getHealth in the API spec.
If the backend is unreachable, the status element reads 'Status: unavailable' instead of staying on 'Checking…' or showing a blank.

assumptions.text: The target directory is empty, so the stack is proposed: vanilla HTML/JS served by a dependency-free Node server.
The browser calls the backend directly (cross-origin). The backend sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so no proxy is needed.
assumptions.source: Backend server.js sets a CORS header; context gives backend_base_url http://127.0.0.1:8000

assumptions.text: The frontend serves on 127.0.0.1:5173. The port can be overridden with the PORT env var.
assumptions.source: Proposed; no port was specified in the requirements or configuration

assumptions.text: The status is fetched once, on page load. Auto-refresh and a manual refresh button are not required.
assumptions.source: HEALTH-1 only says the page 'shows that status'

assumptions.text: An error state ('Status: unavailable') is shown when the call fails. This is added so the page never shows a misleading status. It does not change what the page shows in the success case HEALTH-1 describes.
